# SOP-P2-L4-04 Shift handover - Heat Treat line
Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-RR01, EQ-P2-L4-HT02, EQ-P2-L4-HP03  

Purpose
This procedure defines the required actions, checks, and records for shift-to-shift handover on the Heat Treat line to maintain product quality, machine integrity, and safety continuity. It applies to operators, lead technicians, and maintenance staff assigned to P2-L4. See related documents ECN-2026-042, SB-1016, SOP-P2-L4-01 for engineering changes, safety bulletins, and upstream receiving handover references.

Background and rationale
A structured handover reduces the risk of lost information, missed maintenance items, and process drift. The Heat Treat line contains multiple assets with tight mechanical interfaces. Explicit verification of critical fastener torques and process readiness at shift change prevents component loosening and misalignment that can lead to quality escapes or equipment damage. Examples: confirm radial ring rolling mill mandrel clamp torque after clamp servicing; confirm hydraulic press main ram anchorage after die changes.

Required records and permanence
- Shift Handover Log: operator name in, operator name out, time in/out, summary of condition, anomalies, corrective actions taken.
- Equipment Status Tags: attach or update tags on EQ-P2-L4-RR01, EQ-P2-L4-HT02, EQ-P2-L4-HP03 if equipment is in abnormal state.
- Torque Verification Record: record verified torque values and verifier initials when relevant fasteners are checked.
All records shall be retained according to document retention rules in SOP-P2-L4-01 and filed to the line binder and electronic document control per ECN-2026-042.

Prerequisites (must be satisfied before handover)
1. Incoming operator has completed required qualifications listed in SOP-P2-L4-01 and read applicable sections of SB-1016.
2. Any in-progress maintenance must be documented on the Maintenance Work Order and handed over directly between technicians if work will continue across the shift boundary.
3. All hazardous energy isolation points must be validated and documented in the Lockout/Tagout section of SB-1016 before any physical checks.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
1. At minimum, wear the line standard PPE as specified in SB-1016. This includes hearing protection, eye protection, steel-toe footwear, and gloves suitable for mechanical inspection tasks.
2. Use insulated gloves when handling or verifying electrical lockouts per SB-1016.
3. Use face shield when observing live operations that present splash, chip, or arc hazards as described in SB-1016.

Step-by-step handover procedure
1. Initial briefing
   1.1. Outgoing operator briefs incoming operator at the machine area with the Shift Handover Log visible.
   1.2. Discuss production status, parts in process, next order priorities, and any deviations from standard process parameters noted during the shift.
   1.3. Highlight any vendor parts, tooling, or consumables that arrived or were used and list the exact location.

2. Safety and energy state verification
   2.1. Confirm that all stored energy sources are identified and that status matches tags on energy isolation points.
   2.2. Verify that emergency stop circuits are functional by confirming resets have been performed and that no residual faults exist.

3. Equipment status and critical checks
   3.1. EQ-P2-L4-RR01: Inspect mandrel clamp assembly. Confirm clamp condition, absence of excessive wear, and verify mandrel clamp bolt torque for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01) is 525 N·m. Record verification on the Torque Verification Record along with verifier initials.
   3.2. EQ-P2-L4-HP03: Inspect main ram anchorage and surrounding frame. Verify the main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is 1575 N·m. Record verification on the Torque Verification Record along with verifier initials.
   3.3. EQ-P2-L4-HT02: Confirm heater elements and thermocouples report stable status in the operator interface and that any previous temperature alarms have been cleared and logged in the Shift Handover Log.

4. Process and product check
   4.1. Review last produced parts on the conveyor or in the inspection area. Confirm they meet dimensional and visual criteria and that nonconforming parts are isolated with correction notes attached.
   4.2. If an in-process lot is incomplete, state remaining quantity and next steps in the Shift Handover Log and verify setup for continuity.

5. Maintenance and parts
   5.1. Review open maintenance actions for the line and confirm priority items with maintenance planner per SOP-P2-L4-01.
   5.2. If spare parts or special tools were used, confirm replacements are onboard or ordered and update the log.

6. Communications and escalation
   6.1. Document unresolved issues and the recommended escalation path in the Shift Handover Log.
   6.2. For unresolved safety or equipment faults that could impact production or create an unsafe condition, contact maintenance and lead per SB-1016 immediately and log the contact.

Examples of typical handover entries
- "EQ-P2-L4-RR01 clamp torque checked; 525 N·m verified; no play detected; signed."
- "EQ-P2-L4-HP03 ram bolt torque verified 1575 N·m; frame inspected for cracks; none found; signed."
- "In-process lot # on skid; 10 parts remaining; continue next shift with current setup."

Rationale for torque checks
Torque checks on critical fasteners prevent progressive loosening under cyclic loading. Verifying the exact specified torque ensures clamping forces remain within the designed friction envelope, preventing mandrel slip or ram misalignment that could cause die failure or part rework.

Handover completion and sign-off
1. Both outgoing and incoming operators shall complete the Shift Handover Log entries, including a brief description of the equipment state and any actions pending.
2. The incoming operator signs to accept responsibility for the line and confirms that all required checks were performed or that pending actions were documented and communicated.
3. Retain completed log and Torque Verification Record in the line binder and scan to the electronic folder as required by SOP-P2-L4-01 and ECN-2026-042.

Audit and continuous improvement
Periodic audits of handover records will be conducted to ensure compliance with this procedure and to identify recurring issues. Findings will reference ECN-2026-042 for corrective actions and SB-1016 for safety-related observations.
